import { serverSupabaseClient } from "#supabase/server";
import { PRODUCT_SELECT, withImageUrl } from "~~/server/utils/productImage";
import { productListQuerySchema } from "~~/shared/utils/productSchema";

export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const client = await serverSupabaseClient(event);

  const parsed = productListQuerySchema.safeParse(getQuery(event));
  if (!parsed.success) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: "Invalid query" });
  }
  const { search, category, page, limit, sort } = parsed.data;

  let query = client
    .from("products")
    .select(PRODUCT_SELECT, { count: "exact" });

  if (search) {
    const term = search.replace(/[\\%_]/g, "\\$&");
    query = query.ilike("title", `%${term}%`);
  }

  if (category) {
    query = query.eq("category.slug", category);
  }

  switch (sort) {
    case "oldest":
      query = query.order("created_at", { ascending: true });
      break;
    case "price_asc":
      query = query.order("price", { ascending: true });
      break;
    case "price_desc":
      query = query.order("price", { ascending: false });
      break;
    case "title":
      query = query.order("title", { ascending: true });
      break;
    default:
      query = query.order("created_at", { ascending: false });
  }

  const from = (page - 1) * limit;
  const { data, error, count } = await query.range(from, from + limit - 1);

  if (error) {
    console.error("products.list:", error.code, error.message);
    throw createError({
      statusCode: 500,
      statusMessage: "Failed to load products",
    });
  }

  return {
    items: data.map((row) => withImageUrl(client, row)),
    total: count ?? 0,
    page,
    limit,
  };
});

  const { body, file } = await parseProductForm(event, storeProductSchema);

    .select("id")
    .eq("id", body.category_id)
    .maybeSingle();

    console.error("products.post.category:", categoryError.code, categoryError.message);
    throw createError({ statusCode: 500, statusMessage: "Failed to create product" });
  }
  if (!category) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: "Category not found" });
  }

  const imagePath = file ? await uploadProductImage(admin, file) : null;

  try {
    const data = await writeWithUniqueSlug(
      body.title,

        admin
          .from("products")
          .insert({

            slug,
            description: body.description || null,
            price: body.price,
            stock: body.stock,
            category_id: body.category_id,
            image: imagePath,

          .single(),
      "product",
    );

      throw createError({ statusCode: 500, statusMessage: "Failed to create product" });
    }

    return withImageUrl(admin, data);

Bikin file [slug].put.ts di dalam folder server/api/products, lalu isi file tsb dengan code:

import { parseProductForm } from "~~/server/utils/productForm";
import {
  PRODUCT_SELECT,
  removeProductImage,
  uploadProductImage,
  withImageUrl,
} from "~~/server/utils/productImage";
import {
  productSlugSchema,
  updateProductSchema,
} from "~~/shared/utils/productSchema";

export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const { admin } = await requireAdmin(event);

  const parsedSlug = productSlugSchema.safeParse(getRouterParam(event, "slug"));
  if (!parsedSlug.success) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: "Invalid slug" });
  }

  const { body, file, removeImage } = await parseProductForm(event, updateProductSchema);

  // Produk yang akan diubah (judul dan slug lama dibutuhkan untuk perbandingan)
  const { data: existing, error: findError } = await admin
    .from("products")
    .select("id, title, slug, image")
    .eq("slug", parsedSlug.data)
    .maybeSingle();

  if (findError) {
    console.error("products.put.find:", findError.code, findError.message);
    throw createError({ statusCode: 500, statusMessage: "Failed to update product" });
  }
  if (!existing) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 404, statusMessage: "Product not found" });
  }

  const { data: category, error: categoryError } = await admin
    .from("categories")
    .select("id")
    .eq("id", body.category_id)
    .maybeSingle();

  if (categoryError) {
    console.error("products.put.category:", categoryError.code, categoryError.message);
    throw createError({ statusCode: 500, statusMessage: "Failed to update product" });
  }
  if (!category) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: "Category not found" });
  }

  const newImagePath = file ? await uploadProductImage(admin, file) : null;

  const fields: Record<string, unknown> = {
    title: body.title,
    description: body.description || null,
    price: body.price,
    stock: body.stock,
    category_id: body.category_id,
    updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
  };

  // Prioritas: upload baru > hapus gambar > biarkan gambar lama
  if (newImagePath) fields.image = newImagePath;
  else if (removeImage) fields.image = null;

  const write = (slug: string) =>
    admin
      .from("products")
      .update({ ...fields, slug })
      .eq("id", existing.id)
      .select(PRODUCT_SELECT)
      .maybeSingle();

  let data;
  try {
    if (existing.title === body.title) {
      // Judul sama: slug tidak disentuh
      const result = await write(existing.slug);
      if (result.error) {
        console.error("products.put:", result.error.code, result.error.message);
        throw createError({ statusCode: 500, statusMessage: "Failed to update product" });
      }
      data = result.data;
    } else {
      // Judul berubah: slug dibuat ulang (akhiran acak kalau bentrok)
      data = await writeWithUniqueSlug(body.title, write, "product");
    }
  } catch (e) {
    await removeProductImage(admin, newImagePath); // rollback file baru
    throw e;
  }

  if (!data) {
    await removeProductImage(admin, newImagePath);
    throw createError({ statusCode: 404, statusMessage: "Product not found" });
  }

  // Update sukses -> baru aman hapus gambar lama
  if (existing.image && (newImagePath || removeImage)) {
    await removeProductImage(admin, existing.image);
  }

  return withImageUrl(admin, data);
});

import { removeProductImage } from "~~/server/utils/productImage";
import { productSlugSchema } from "~~/shared/utils/productSchema";

export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const { admin } = await requireAdmin(event);

  const parsed = productSlugSchema.safeParse(getRouterParam(event, "slug"));
  if (!parsed.success) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: "Invalid slug" });
  }

  const { data, error } = await admin
    .from("products")
    .delete()
    .eq("slug", parsed.data)
    .select("id, image");

  if (error) {
    console.error("products.delete:", error.code, error.message);
    throw createError({
      statusCode: 500,
      statusMessage: "Failed to delete product",
    });
  }

  if (data.length === 0) {
    throw createError({ statusCode: 404, statusMessage: "Product not found" });
  }

  // Row sudah terhapus -> bersihkan file di storage.
  await removeProductImage(admin, data[0]!.image);

  return { deleted: true };
});

5. Product Composable

Kita membutuhkan fungsi-fungsi yang berisi logika untuk memanipulasi data (CRUD). Fungsi2 tersebut akan kita satukan ke dalam 1 composable.

Bikin file useProductAction.ts di dalam folder app/composables/, lalu isi file tersebut dengan code berikut:

import ModalConfirm from "~/components/modal/Confirm.vue";
import {
  PRODUCT_IMAGE_MAX_SIZE,
  PRODUCT_IMAGE_MIME_TYPES,
  type ProductPayload,
} from "~~/shared/utils/productSchema";

export const useProductAction = () => {
  const toast = useToast();
  const overlay = useOverlay();
  const confirmModal = overlay.create(ModalConfirm);

  function validateImage(file: File) {
    if (!(PRODUCT_IMAGE_MIME_TYPES as readonly string[]).includes(file.type)) {
      throw new Error("Only JPEG, PNG, or WebP images are allowed");
    }
    if (file.size > PRODUCT_IMAGE_MAX_SIZE) {
      throw new Error("Image must be 2 MB or smaller");
    }
  }

  function buildFormData(payload: ProductPayload) {
    const form = new FormData();
    form.append("title", payload.title);
    form.append("description", payload.description ?? "");
    form.append("price", String(payload.price));
    form.append("stock", String(payload.stock));
    form.append("category_id", payload.category_id);

    if (payload.image) {
      validateImage(payload.image);
      form.append("image", payload.image);
    }
    if (payload.removeImage) form.append("remove_image", "true");

    return form;
  }

  // Jangan set Content-Type manual: $fetch + FormData otomatis menambahkan boundary.
  async function createProduct(payload: ProductPayload) {
    await $fetch("/api/products", {
      method: "POST",
      body: buildFormData(payload),
    });
    toast.add({
      title: "Success: Product Created",
      color: "success",
      id: "modal-success",
    });
  }

  async function updateProduct(slug: string, payload: ProductPayload) {
    await $fetch(`/api/products/${encodeURIComponent(slug)}`, {
      method: "PUT",
      body: buildFormData(payload),
    });
    toast.add({
      title: "Success: Product Updated",
      color: "success",
      id: "modal-success",
    });
  }

  async function deleteProduct({
    title,
    slug,
    refreshAction,
  }: {
    title: string;
    slug: string;
    refreshAction: () => void;
  }) {
    const instance = confirmModal.open({
      title: `Delete ${title}`,
      description: `Are you sure you want to delete the product "${title}"? This also removes its image.`,
    });

    if (!(await instance.result)) {
      toast.add({
        title: "Delete the product cancelled",
        color: "neutral",
        id: "modal-dismiss",
      });
      return;
    }

    try {
      await $fetch(`/api/products/${encodeURIComponent(slug)}`, {
        method: "DELETE",
      });
      refreshAction();
      toast.add({
        title: "Successfully delete the product",
        color: "success",
        id: "modal-success",
      });
    } catch (error: any) {
      toast.add({
        title: `Fail: ${error?.data?.statusMessage ?? "Something went wrong"}`,
        color: "error",
        id: "modal-dismiss",
      });
    }
  }

  return { createProduct, updateProduct, deleteProduct, validateImage };
};

6. Tambah kolom slug di tabel product

Pada project resto di supabase, buka menu SQL Editor, lalu paste blok ini, pastikan run 1x aja:

alter table public.products add column slug text;

update public.products
set slug =
  left(
    coalesce(
      nullif(trim(both '-' from regexp_replace(lower(title), '[^a-z0-9]+', '-', 'g')), ''),
      'product'
    ),
    90
  ) || '-' || left(id::text, 6)
where slug is null;

alter table public.products add constraint products_slug_key unique (slug);

commit;

medium.resumo: Mobile layout, column summaries, and live updates in the MIT core. Swimlanes and group manager in PRO.
medium.conteudo_html:
Mobile layout, column summaries, and live updates in the MIT core. Swimlanes and group manager in PRO.

A Kanban board looks simple until a real team starts using one: someone opens it on a phone, two people edit the same board at once, a project needs lanes for teams, not just columns for stages.

SVAR Kanban 2.7 for React, Vue, and Svelte addresses these cases, giving you a ready-to-use tool to build custom task boards for a wide range of scenarios. Here is what version 2.7 adds and why it makes the component a robust base for workflow management apps.

What’s New in the MIT Core

The component comes with a free, open-source core that helps you create drag-and-drop Kanban boards with a solid feature set. Here is what version 2.7 adds to the free version:

A layout for phones

Side-by-side columns don’t fit small screens at 375px. The new stack layout puts all columns into one vertical list, each with its own header:

<Kanban {cards} {columns} render={{ layout: "stack" }} />

There is no auto mode: your app decides when to switch, for example with a matchMedia listener. One limit to know about: cards can’t be dragged in stack mode, because a finger on a card scrolls the board. Moving a card goes through the editor or a menu.

Column summaries

Version 2.6 had cardLimit, a per-column cap that showed the card count and flagged overflow. With this update, you can define what the column header shows: a card count, a total estimate, the number of high-priority tasks, or any value derived from the cards:

const summaries = [{
  id: "effort",
  calculate: cards =>
    cards.reduce((sum, card) => sum + (card.estimateHours ?? 0), 0),
  format: value => (value ? `${value} h` : ""),
  css: value => (value > 40 ? "effort-over-capacity" : ""),
}];

The board recalculates summaries after every card change, filter, or sort.

Menus and dynamic columns

Card and column menus (action buttons and right-click) come as ready-made components, with built-in edit, duplicate, and delete options. Menu items can be a static list or a function that runs when the menu opens, so they can reflect the state of the card or column.

Columns no longer have to be static config. Omit the columns array, and the board creates one column for each distinct value that columnAccessor reads from the cards:

<Kanban {cards} columnAccessor="status" />

This suits prototypes and read-only boards built over data you don’t control. Inferred columns are rebuilt on every card change, so empty columns disappear. For an editable board with fixed stages, keep an explicit columns array.

To change columns while the app is running, use the new column actions:

api.exec("add-column", {
    column: { id: "review", label: "Review" },
    before: "done",
});
api.exec("move-column", { id: "backlog" }); // moves to the end
api.exec("delete-column", { id: "review" });

These actions change only the column configuration. Cards from a deleted column stay in the data and reappear when a column with the same ID is added back. Columns can also have their own width, so a wide backlog can sit next to a narrow “Done” column.

Live updates

For shared boards, KanbanEventBridge listens to a server-sent events stream and applies remote changes locally: a card someone drags in another tab appears in yours, with summaries already recalculated.

What’s New in PRO

The MIT core covers the board itself. PRO is for boards that have grown past a side project: more structure, more data, more people working in the same place. Version 2.7 adds four features.

Swimlanes

Columns answer “what stage is this in?” Swimlanes answer “whose is it?” Each lane is a horizontal row, for example one per team, project, or customer, and every card belongs to both a column and a lane:

<Kanban {cards} {columns} {swimlanes} swimlaneAccessor="team" />

Users can drag cards between lanes and collapse the lanes they don’t need. Filtering, sorting, and summaries work the same as on a board without lanes, and swimlanes also work in the stack layout on phones.

Group manager

GroupManager is a ready-made panel where users add, rename, reorder, and delete columns and swimlanes. It can sit in a sidebar:

<GroupManager {api} placement="sidebar" onclose={() => (open = false)} />

The panel never moves or deletes cards, and it shows how many cards each group holds. If cards still refer to a deleted group, one click restores it. Every edit goes through the regular actions, so RestDataProvider saves it like any other change.

Drag-in from outside the board

With cardProjection, users can drag items from a backlog list or search results straight into a column. Your app handles the native drag events. The board finds the drop target, shows a preview, and gives you the destination column and swimlane. On drop, you dispatch add-card.

Card grid

Set cardWidth and cardHeight on a column and its cards become fixed-size tiles in a grid:

{ id: "design", label: "Design", width: 480, cardWidth: 220, cardHeight: 140 }

A wider column fits more tiles per row. It works well when cards are visual rather than text-heavy: design reviews, candidate shortlists, content calendars, backlogs with image previews.

Some Breaking Changes

2.7 removes cardLimit and overLimit. Use a column summary with your own wipLimit key instead. The full list of breaking changes is in the release article.

Get started

The code above uses Svelte syntax. The React and Vue editions share the same API model.

You can install the free, MIT-licensed edition of SVAR Kanban via npm — just choose your framework:

npm install @svar-ui/react-kanban
npm install @svar-ui/vue-kanban
npm install @svar-ui/svelte-kanban

PRO comes with a 30-day trial for each framework.

For demos, the full changelog, and every feature in detail, read the full release article, or find SVAR Kanban on GitHub: React • Vue • Svelte

Quarta-feira | 25 de novembro de 2026

Com o fechamento da temporada de grandes maratonas brasileiras, uma análise dos números de 2026 revela o cenário atual da distância no país. No total, as 10 maiores provas somaram 51.400 concluintes. A Maratona do Rio de Janeiro mantém uma liderança isolada com 14.175 atletas, quase o dobro da segunda colocada, a Maratona de Porto Alegre, que teve 7.518 concluintes e um crescimento de 30% em relação a 2025.

O maior salto proporcional foi da NB42K Porto Alegre, que cresceu absurdos 192,4% em apenas um ano, chegando a 5.161 concluintes e se firmando no top 4.

“Confira o ranking completo das 10 maiores maratonas do Brasil em 2026:”
1. “Maratona do Rio:” 14.175 concluintes (+7.9%)
2. “Maratona de Porto Alegre:” 7.518 concluintes (+30.3%)
3. “SP City Marathon:” 6.635 concluintes (+22.8%)
4. “NB42K Porto Alegre:” 5.161 concluintes (+192.4%)
5. “Maratona Internacional de SP:” 4.845 concluintes (+0.5%)
6. “Maratona de Florianópolis:” 3.614 concluintes (-29.7%)
7. “Maratona de Curitiba:” 2.759 concluintes (-9.2%)
8. “Maratona de Belo Horizonte:” 2.393 concluintes (estreia)
9. “Maratona do Paraná:” 2.275 concluintes (estreia)
10. “Maratona Monumental de Brasília:” 2.060 concluintes (+11.8%)

Crescimento das Maratonas desde 2023

Analisando a evolução desde 2023, o primeiro ano com um calendário completo de maratonas após a pandemia, o crescimento de algumas provas é notável. O maior ganho absoluto foi da Maratona do Rio, que adicionou mais de 7 mil atletas desde 2023, um aumento de 97,8%.

Em termos de expansão relativa, a Maratona Monumental de Brasília quase triplicou de tamanho, crescendo 195,6% em três anos. A NB42K Porto Alegre, desde sua estreia em 2024, já cresceu 318%. Outras provas que mais que dobraram de tamanho desde 2023 foram a SP City Marathon (+103%) e a Maratona de Porto Alegre (+84,2%). As estreantes Maratona de Belo Horizonte e Maratona do Paraná, junto com a NB42K Porto Alegre, já entraram direto no Top 10.

Calendário 2027 do Mountain Do

O circuito Mountain Do já divulgou as datas de suas provas para 2027, com etapas que passam por cinco países. O calendário inclui destinos como Colônia do Sacramento (Uruguai), Praia do Rosa (SC), Deserto da Namíbia, Chapada dos Veadeiros (GO), Costão do Santinho (SC), Fim do Mundo em Ushuaia (Argentina), Fernando de Noronha (PE), Selva Amazônica em Macapá (AP), Deserto do Saara (Marrocos) e Pantanal (MS). Para quem se interessar, o cupom “CORRIDANOAR” oferece 10% de desconto em todas as etapas, incluindo as internacionais.

Assessoria de Sorocaba usa patinete como “diferencial”

Uma assessoria esportiva de Sorocaba, a MoodRun, gerou polêmica ao divulgar como “novidade” e “diferencial” o uso de um patinete elétrico por um treinador para acompanhar e fornecer hidratação aos seus atletas durante as provas. A prática, no entanto, é irregular e proibida pela maioria dos regulamentos de corrida, que vetam o auxílio de terceiros ou o uso de recursos tecnológicos sem autorização prévia da organização. Além de ser uma infração, a presença de um patinete no percurso coloca em risco a segurança dos demais corredores. O correto seria a assessoria montar pontos fixos de apoio para seus atletas, como é prática comum e permitida.

Circuito Brasil Gigante define datas

O circuito Brasil Gigante já fechou as datas de suas oito maratonas para 2027. A jornada começa com a Maratona do Paraná, em Guaratuba, no dia 28 de março. O calendário segue com São Paulo (abril), Porto Alegre (junho), Campo Grande (julho), João Pessoa (agosto), Florianópolis (agosto), Salvador (setembro) e Aracaju (outubro). Os corredores que completarem as oito maratonas, sem limite de tempo, receberão uma mandala especial.

Uma das grandes novidades é a mudança no percurso da Maratona Internacional da Cidade de João Pessoa. A largada agora será no Centro Histórico, na Praça do Bispo, e o trajeto terá altimetria negativa, descendo em direção à orla para terminar no Busto de Tamandaré. Além disso, a Maratona Internacional de Aracaju já abriu as inscrições para a edição de 2027.

Fla Run acontece no Aterro do Flamengo

Neste domingo, 29 de novembro, acontece a Fla Run, a corrida oficial do Flamengo. A prova será realizada no Aterro do Flamengo, com percursos de 3, 5 e 10 km. Ainda dá tempo de se inscrever para participar do evento rubro-negro. Use o cupom “CORRIDANOAR10” para garantir 10% de desconto na sua inscrição.
